key_insight: Introduce a compact, trajectory-level strategy as an explicit latent that is sampled to guide agentic RL (e.g., LLM agents), improving exploration and credit assignment across long-horizon tasks.
problem_solved: Reactive, step-by-step policies struggle with exploration and credit assignment over extended trajectories; StraTA addresses the lack of an explicit, learnable high-level plan that can steer behavior across an entire episode.
method: Sample a compact trajectory-level strategy at episode start (a high-level latent/plan) that conditions downstream action selection.
Train the agent so low-level actions are encouraged to follow the sampled strategy via conditioning and incentive/auxiliary objectives, improving credit assignment to strategy-level choices.
Optimize both strategy sampling and the conditional policy end-to-end (hierarchical/latent-conditioned RL), yielding better long-horizon exploration and behavior coherence.
impact: Provides a simple, model-agnostic way to add strategic planning to agentic LLMs and RL agents, improving long-horizon performance and interpretability with minimal architecture changes.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: strategy sampler -> conditional policy -> environment -> rewards, showing the strategy persists across the trajectory.
Trajectory timeline: episode segmented by a single sampled strategy with arrows illustrating improved credit assignment from end reward back to the strategy.
Hierarchical block diagram: high-level strategy latent above low-level policy, indicating information flow and training signals.
Performance sketch: bar/line chart comparing baseline reactive agent vs StraTA on long-horizon metrics (exploration success, final-task reward).
paper_title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
paper_authors: Xiangyuan Xue, Yifan Zhou, Zidong Wang, Shengji Tang, Philip Torr
